planting.note: Start indoors in warmth; celosia needs steady heat to grow well. Cramer's Series is a commercial cut-flower breeding line valued for exceptionally heavy stem counts per plant, developed for flower farmers who need consistent, long-lasting cut stems through the heat of summer.

directions: Start seed indoors in warm conditions a few weeks before the last frost and transplant only after the soil is warm; Cramer's Rose is part of a commercial cut-flower celosia series bred specifically for flower farmers, prized for throwing an unusually high number of long, sturdy stems per plant compared with older cockscomb varieties. Each stem carries a dense, velvety, brain-like crested bloom in a rich rose-pink that holds its color and form for weeks both in the garden and in fresh or dried arrangements. Give it full sun, consistent warmth, and well-drained soil, and keep harvesting stems regularly through the summer to encourage the plant to keep pushing new ones — celosia thrives on heat and shrugs off the worst of a Gulf South summer better than most cut flowers.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Kees' Orange is a Dutch-bred African marigold selection valued for its large, fully double, deeply ruffled blooms that hold up unusually well as a cut flower.

directions: Sow directly after frost danger passes or start indoors for a head start, barely covering the seed; Kees' Orange is a large-flowered African marigold selection producing fully double, ruffled, deep-orange pompon blooms on sturdy, well-branched plants that stay more compact than older tall African types like Crackerjack. Plant in full sun where its pungent foliage helps deter nematodes and many garden pests, making it a classic companion plant near tomatoes and vegetables as well as a strong performer in a cut-flower border — the sturdy stems and long vase life make it a favorite for market bouquets. Deadhead spent blooms regularly to keep the plant flowering steadily through the heat of summer into fall.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
